deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of Gauss's mathematical diary (Tagebuch), entries [72]-[80], July-October 1797, Göttingen and then Braunschweig. It contains no worked derivations, only dated statements of results. Each is restated below.

[72] 'Plani possibilitatem demonstravi', Göttingen, 28 July 1797: 'I have proved the possibility of the plane.' This is usually read as a foundations-of-geometry note: constructing or justifying the plane without the parallel postulate. No argument is given.

[73] 1 August 1797. The claim entered on 27 July (previous page: several periods of the roots of x^n=1 cannot have the same form) contained an error. Gauss now settles the matter by proving that no period can be a rational number. In modern terms, take n prime and n-1=ef. A Gaussian period eta = sum of zeta^(g^(ke+j)) over k=0..f-1 has e distinct Galois conjugates, so its minimal polynomial has degree e. For e>1 it is therefore irrational. (This justification is mine, not on the page.) Example: n=7, e=2: eta = zeta+zeta^2+zeta^4 satisfies eta^2+eta+2=0.

[74] Undated. How the signs must be fixed when the number of periods is doubled. When the e periods are split into 2e periods, one solves quadratics, and the signs of the square roots must be chosen consistently (cf. Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §§ 352-365). No details are given.

[75] 26 August 1797. Gauss found the number of 'prime functions' (irreducible polynomials mod p) by the simplest analysis. The modern formula, used in his unpublished Section 8 of the Disquisitiones (Werke II), is N_mu = (1/mu) * sum over d|mu of mobius(d) p^(mu/d). It follows from p^mu = sum over d|mu of d N_d.

[76] 30 August 1797. Theorem: if f = x^mu + a x^(mu-1) + b x^(mu-2) + ... + m is prime (irreducible) mod p, then a + x + x^p + x^(p^2) + ... + x^(p^(mu-1)) is divisible by f mod p. The first written form, with coefficients in increasing powers, is struck through. Modern reading: for a root theta of f in GF(p^mu), the conjugates are theta^(p^i). Hence Tr(theta) = theta + theta^p + ... + theta^(p^(mu-1)) = -a, the sum of the roots. 'Etc. etc.' indicates that the other coefficients come from the higher symmetric functions in the same way.

[77] 31 August 1797. The theorem is proved, and a road to much greater things is paved by introducing multiple (double) moduli. This means computing modulo p and f(x) at once, i.e. in GF(p)[x]/(f), which is arithmetic in a finite field.

[78] 4 September 1797. The result of 1 August is adapted more generally to arbitrary moduli, presumably composite n.

[79] 9 September 1797. Gauss discovered principles by which solving congruences with respect to multiple moduli is reduced to congruences with respect to a linear modulus.

[80] Braunschweig, October 1797. A proof, 'by a genuine method', that equations have (real or) imaginary roots: the fundamental theorem of algebra. A later pencil note reads: 'Prom[ulgatum] in dissert. special. mense Aug. 1799', i.e. published in his doctoral dissertation, Helmstedt 1799.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible; the page only states results.
Grammatical slip in [73]: 'probari possumus' should be 'probare possumus'.

[76] as written takes the polynomial to be monic. The first attempt, in increasing powers '1+ax+bxx+...+mx^mu', was struck out, presumably because the trace formula is cleanest for monic f. In general the constant should be l/m, where l is the coefficient of x^(mu-1) and m the leading coefficient.
[72]: the meaning of 'plani possibilitatem' is not determinable from the page itself; the reading as a foundations-of-geometry claim is conventional.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of Gauss's famous diary, published by Klein in 1903 (Werke X.1) and extensively commented on. The finite-field results and the fundamental theorem of algebra are well documented as Gauss's, with priority over Galois and Dedekind already acknowledged.

transcription_corrections: Line 'Theorema': the struck-out text is probably an initial '1+ax+bxx+...+mx^mu', later intended as the monic form x^mu + a x^(mu-1) + ...
'1+x+x^{p}+x^{pp}+&c x^{p^{mu-1}}' should read 'a + x + x^p + x^pp + &c. x^(p^(mu-1))'; the first symbol is 'a', not '1'.
The struck line '[-1 - b + ax + a-]' is a cancelled draft and not part of the theorem.
'Modulorum multiplicium strata': 'strata' is 'stratā' (a road paved), continuing 'viaque ... per introd[uctionem]'.
Final line 'Prom. in dissert. special. Mense Aug. 1799' is a later pencil addition (Promulgatum).
